summary: _“1) Condone the delay in the commissioning of assets covered under this petition._ 8. The hearings in this matter were held on 27.9.2023, 30.10.2023, and 20.12.2023. The matter was reserved for order on 20.12.2023. However, the order could not be issued prior to the former Members, who formed part of the coram, demitting the office. Accordingly, the matter was heard again on 16.7.2024, and the order was reserved. 10. Having heard the Petitioner’s representatives, the learned counsels for the Petitioner, MPPMCL, MSEDCL, and AWEMPOPL, and having perused the material on record, we proceed to dispose of the Petition. 11. At the outset, MPPMCL has objected to the maintainability of the instant Petition for non-joinder of the necessary party(ies) and misjoinder of constituents of the Western Region, including MPPMCL. To substantiate its argument, MPPMCL has cited a judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Kasturi v. Iyyamperumal [AIR 2005 SC 2813]. The said judgment has laid down a test with two conditions for determining the question, whether a particular party is a necessary party to a proceeding or not; namely, there must be a right to some relief against such party in respect of the matter involved in the proceedings in question; and it should not be possible to pass an effective decree in the absence of such a party. 12. MPPMCL has submitted that both the transmission assets, i.e., Assets I and II, were planned, executed, and implemented for the sale and supply of power to Respondent No. 11, Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL), and the beneficiaries of the Northern Regions. However, the Petitioner has not made UPPCL (in the Northern Region) a party to the Petition, which is the only beneficiary, and instead has arrayed constituents of the Western Region as Respondents in this Petition. MPPMCL has further submitted that the Petitioner has not defined who is/are the beneficiary(ies) of the transmission assets covered in the instant Petition; instead, it has repeatedly used Respondents and the beneficiaries interchangeably. The constituents of the Western Region, including MPPMCL, have nothing to do with the transmission assets covered under the instant Petition and are not beneficiaries of those assets. MPPMCL has, therefore, submitted that the instant Petition is liable to be 14. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and MPPMCL on the issue of non-joinder and misjoinder of the necessary party(ies) to the instant Petition. 15. On perusal of the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of Kasturi v. Iyamperumal recorded in 2005 6 SCC 733, in the context of Order I Rule 9 and Order I Rule 10 (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, has laid down a test for determining whether a particular party is a necessary party to a proceeding. The two conditions laid down by the Hon’ble Supreme Court include the existence of a right to some relief against such party in respect of the controversies involved in the proceedings, and no effective decree can be passed in the absence of such party. 16. On perusal of the record, we note that the Petitioner filed the instant Petition before the Commission, impleading the constituents of the Western Region, including MPPMCL and SBESSSPTPL (now AWEMPOPL) as Respondents. Later, the Petitioner, vide affidavit dated 16.10.2023, submitted a revised Memo of Parties wherein it impleaded AWEMPOPL (formerly SBESSSPTPL) as Respondent No. 10, which is a constituent of the Northern Region. Thereafter, MPPMCL, in its response filed vide affidavit dated 18.10.2023, raised the issue of the instant Petition's maintainability. The issue was also raised before us during the hearing on 30.10.2023. Pursuant to the hearing on 30.10.2023, the Commission directed the Petitioner to implead the constituents of the Northern Region and CTUIL as Respondents and file the amended ‘Memo of Parties’. The directions of the Commission were complied with by the Petitioner, vide its affidavit dated 7.11.2023, wherein it impleaded the constituents of the Northern Region as well as the CTUIL as Respondent Nos. 11 to 25 and 26, respectively, in the amended Memo of Parties. As the necessary parties have been added to the present Petition, there is nothing left to decide regarding the issue of maintainability. The contentions of MPPMCL regarding the sharing of transmission charges have been dealt with in the relevant portion of this order. Therefore, we now proceed to dispose of the Petition on merits. - c.
